items.title: Investment Banker
items.summary: Your strong interests in leading, organizing, and investigating complex problems, all scoring 100, suggest a good fit for this field. Your interest in wealth and status, both at 100, also aligns with the potential rewards of this demanding profession. To pursue this, you would typically study finance, economics, or a related quantitative field in university.
items.market: The financial sector in Saudi Arabia is growing with significant national projects, offering good career growth opportunities.
items.takesLabel: WHAT IT TAKES TO GET THERE
items.takes: As you are currently a student, the main gap is gaining specific knowledge in finance and relevant work experience like internships.
items.now: 1. Taking a free online course in financial markets or investment principles is recommended to understand the basics. — This helps you learn the foundational terms and concepts used in investment banking, which is key for a new field. 2. Speaking with someone who works in the finance industry, perhaps through a university career event, would be a good way to gain insight into the daily work. — Understanding the actual day-to- day life of an investment banker helps you see if it truly matches your expectations and work style preference. 3. Exploring university programs that offer majors in finance, economics, or business administration with a finance focus would be a practical next step for your studies. — A relevant degree is a fundamental requirement for entering the investment banking field and provides the necessary academic foundation.
items.aiTitle: How AI may change this career
evidence: Global evidence: General industry trends indicate that artificial intelligence tools are increasingly used in finance for data analysis, risk assessment, and automating routine reporting. This allows human professionals to focus on higher-level strategy and client interaction.

In your market: This is a general outlook, not verified job-market data. In the GCC, financial institutions are also exploring and adopting AI for efficiency, particularly in areas like market analysis and compliance checks.
items.means: As a university student, it would be helpful to understand how financial data is analyzed and presented. You could consider taking a short online course that covers basic financial modeling and data interpretation.

blocks.t: One small step for this week, then a simple 90-day path, built around your top career match
Built around your top match: Investment Banker
Your first step this week

A good first step is to read three job descriptions for an "Investment Banking Analyst" or "Junior Lawyer" position in Saudi Arabia or another GCC country. Look for roles within a large organization, since you showed interest in such environments. Why: This helps you understand the daily tasks, required skills, and work environment for roles that combine your interest in business (Enterprising) with analytical thinking (Investigative) and structured work (Conventional).
YOU WILL PRODUCE
A short list of 3-5 key tasks and 3-5 required skills from these job descriptions.
WHEN
Within 2 days, about 45 minutes.
Worksheet:

items: Any mention of pace or structure?

blocks.t: Days 2–7

Days 2-3 — We suggest you find and watch two short online videos (5-10 minutes each) that show a "day in the life" of an Investment Banker or a Lawyer. You will produce: A few notes on what surprised you or seemed appealing about each role.

Day 4 — You could identify two university professors, alumni, or family friends who work in finance (like an Investment Banker) or legal fields (like a Lawyer) in the GCC. You will produce: A short list with their names and contact information, if available.

Days 5-6 — It would help to draft a short email to one of the people on your list from Day 4, asking if they would be open to a 15-minute informational chat about their career path as a student exploring options. Do not send it yet. You will produce: A draft email.

Day 7 — A good way to end the week is to review what you produced and pick the next step. Consider which career (Investment Banker or Lawyer) felt more interesting after your initial research and whether you want to try to send your draft email. You will produce: A decision on which career path to explore further next week, and whether to send the email.
Your next 90 days

Weeks 2–4 — Build momentum If you found the Investment Banker or Lawyer roles interesting, it would be helpful to send the informational email you drafted and try to have one or two short conversations with professionals in those fields.
You could also look for short, free online courses (lasting a few hours) related to financial modeling or legal research to see if you enjoy the foundational tasks of an Investment Banker or Lawyer.
It would be wise to update your CV or resume to highlight your academic strengths and any club or volunteer leadership experience, preparing it for future internship applications.

Months 2–3 — Build Consider searching for entry-level or student internships in the finance or legal departments of large organizations in Saudi Arabia or the wider GCC. This would give you practical experience related to roles like Investment Banker or Lawyer.
You might want to explore other matched careers, such as a Real Estate Agent or a Military Officer, by looking up their daily duties and required qualifications in the GCC.

It is recommended to seek out a mentor or advisor, perhaps through your university, who can offer guidance on career paths in fields that align with your Enterprising, Conventional, and Investigative interests.
Your skills to build and practice exercise: Investment Banker
SKILLS TO BUILD

Critical analysis of AI-generated reports — Investment banking relies on accurate and insightful analysis, and while AI can quickly generate reports, the ability to critically review, question, and refine these outputs is crucial.

Strategic client communication — AI can draft basic messages, but the nuanced art of advising clients, understanding their deeper needs, and building long-term trust requires human communication skills.
PRACTICE EXERCISE

A good exercise would be to find a recent financial news article about a company that interests you. Then, use a free AI tool to create a short summary of the article and list three potential investment risks for that company. After that, review the AI's summary and risks. Identify any information the AI missed, misinterpreted, or any risks it overlooked. Based on your review, draft a short, clear email to a hypothetical client explaining one key risk you identified, making sure your language is easy to understand and builds trust, rather than just repeating what the AI said.
YOU WILL HAVE
You will have the original news article, the AI-generated summary and risk list, your notes highlighting the AI's strengths and weaknesses, and your personally drafted client email.

items.title: Financial Modeling & Valuation Analyst (FMVA)
items.about: What it is about: This certification teaches industry-standard financial modeling and how to value companies using Excel.
items.why: Investment bankers often use financial models and valuation methods, and this course gives you those important skills.

items.title: Islamic Finance and Banking
items.about: What it is about: This course covers the basics of banking that follows Shariah law and Islamic financial tools.
items.why: In Saudi Arabia, understanding Islamic finance is very useful for an investment banker to advise clients correctly.

items.title: Emotional Intelligence
items.about: What it is about: This course helps you build self-awareness, understand others' feelings, and manage relationships.
items.why: A sports coach needs to understand and manage emotions well, both their own and those of their team members.

items.title: Mental Health First Aid
items.about: What it is about: This course teaches you to spot and respond to mental health issues in the workplace.
items.why: A sports coach often supports the overall well-being of athletes, and knowing about mental health can be very helpful for this.

items.title: Real Estate Finance and Investment
items.about: What it is about: This course covers how to value, fund, and analyze investments in real estate.
items.why: A real estate agent benefits from knowing how properties are valued and financed to better help clients buy and sell.

items.title: Entrepreneurship Specialization
items.about: What it is about: This course covers everything from testing a business idea to growing a new company, including funding and strategy.
items.why: Many real estate agents work for themselves, so learning about running a business can help them succeed in their work.

items.title: Contract Law
items.about: What it is about: This course covers the main ideas of how contracts are made, enforced, and what happens if they are broken.
items.why: Understanding contract law is a basic skill for a lawyer, as many legal tasks involve contracts.

items.title: Negotiation Mastery
items.about: What it is about: This course teaches practical ways to negotiate and resolve disagreements.
items.why: Lawyers often need to negotiate on behalf of their clients, and this course helps build those key skills.
